podcast.body: An obscure orchestral cover version of this song, recorded sometime in the mid-1960s, was sampled for 4.5 seconds in The Verve's "Bitter Sweet Symphony." "Much of Bitter Sweet Symphony is built around a 4.5 second sample from an orchestral version of a Rolling Stones song called The Last Time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 2

podcast.body: The original version of this song, released in 1965, did not contain the six-second string figure later featured in The Andrew Loog Oldham Orchestra's 1966 easy-listening version. The original also heavily borrowed from "This Could Be the Last Time" by The Staple Singers. "That six-second string figure does not appear in the original version of The Last Time by the Rolling Stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, originally released in 1965, was covered by the Andrew Loog Oldham Orchestra in their 1965 album *The Rolling Stones Songbook*. A five-note progression from Oldham's orchestral interpretation later inspired The Verve's "Bittersweet Symphony." Due to a subsequent legal dispute, Mick Jagger and Keith Richards ultimately gained 100% of the publishing rights and royalties from The Verve's song. "On this record was Andrew Luege Oldham's interpretation of the Stone Song the last time from 1965."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
